transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-05
Start time: 15:20 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (BetaBank - Head of Vendor Risk), Anita Desai (BetaBank - Security Engineer), Rajiv Kapoor (BetaBank - Procurement)

Summary (auto):
Redwood walks BetaBank through the SIG/CAIQ-style vendor risk questionnaire. Focus on SOC 2 evidence, RBAC/SSO integrations, audit/logging capabilities, data residency options, and encryption/KMS workflows. Customer requests redacted SOC 2, network diagrams, and confirmation on HSM/KMS support for private deployments. Next steps and evidence upload responsibilities agreed.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we should do quick intros and then walk through the questionnaire, does that work?
[00:08] Michael Torres: yep, that sounds good, Michael here, head of vendor risk at BetaBank, I'll be the primary reviewer for the SIG pack.
[00:13] Anita Desai: Anita, security eng, I'll be following the technical bits, especially encryption and logs.
[00:18] Rajiv Kapoor: Rajiv from procurement, i'll handle contracts and evidence intake.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: great—Jordan from Redwood AE and with me is Priya, our SE who handles audits and private deployments.
[00:29] Priya Menon: hi all, thanks, I'll try to keep answers practical and point to artifacts as we go.

[02:00] Jordan Lee: ok first slide, we have the SIG-lite questions your team sent. we'll go question by question, call out any requested attachments like SOC 2, network diagrams, and where evidence will live. any initial constraints we should know about? data residency or on-prem requirements?
[02:15] Michael Torres: yes data residency is a big one for us, primary workloads must stay in the US-East region, some consumer PII must be stored within our approved regions only. also we require SOC 2 type II evidence and a network diagram for any private deployment.
[02:30] Priya Menon: understood, we can scope hosted vs private — our hosted API can be region-restricted to us-east on our cloud, and for Private we have VPC/on-prem packaging. For encryption we support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations for private installs.

[04:10] Anita Desai: when you say KMS, is that the ability to bring your own key material and have the keys never leave HSM? we need attestable separation for certain regulated models.
[04:20] Priya Menon: yes, for Private we integrate with external KMS solutions and HSMs. for hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS in supported clouds; keys are never exported. i'll add a note to provide our KMS integration doc.

[06:05] Michael Torres: can we get that in writing in the SIG answers — like the exact supported KMS providers and any limitations?
[06:12] Jordan Lee: yes we'll list supported KMS vendors, caveats for model caching, and any small latency impacts. We'll flag sections that require legal redaction or cannot be shared.

[08:00] Rajiv Kapoor: procurement question — we often need proof of SOC 2 and remediation timelines, do you have a standard evidence bundle?
[08:10] Priya Menon: we do. we'll upload a redacted SOC 2 Type II, summary control matrix mapping to SIG controls, and a secure link to the auditor's letter. we'll also include audit log retention policies and sample logs.

[10:30] Anita Desai: about audit logs — does Redwood provide tenant-level immutable logs and can we export them to our SIEM?
[10:40] Priya Menon: yes, we provide per-tenant audit logs with an append-only design; customers can push logs to S3 or a syslog endpoint. we also provide event streaming to third-party SIEMs, and the console has log export controls.
[11:15] Michael Torres: retention windows? default and maximum?
[11:20] Priya Menon: default 90 days in the hosted plan, upgradeable to 2 years with add-on retention. for Dedicated/Private you can set retention according to your policies — it's configurable because you control storage.

[13:05] Jordan Lee: moving to access controls — RBAC and SSO, we support SAML2.0/SAML with IdP integrations and SCIM for provisioning. Priya, any notes on role mappings?
[13:18] Priya Menon: yes we surface RBAC roles in the console, can map IdP groups to roles via SCIM, and we have fine-grained API keys and token scopes. we also support audit trails for role changes.

[15:00] Anita Desai: is there support for credential rotation and automatic key rollover?
[15:05] Priya Menon: yes API keys can be rotated; for KMS keys rotation policies depend on the provider but we support scheduled rotations and advise customers to rotate service keys regularly. we can demonstrate the process in the follow-up.

[17:30] Michael Torres: on the questionnaire there's a question about encryption in transit and at rest, plus column asking for encryption algorithms used. can you provide specifics?
[17:40] Priya Menon: in transit we use TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers, and at rest we use AES-256. For private deployments you can inject your own encryption stack. we'll attach a crypto spec doc with exact cipher suites and versions.

[19:50] Rajiv Kapoor: another contractual ask — do you support subprocessor lists and notification windows for changes?
[20:00] Jordan Lee: yes we maintain an up-to-date subprocessor list and a 30-day notification window for major changes; we can include that as evidence.

[21:40] Anita Desai: regarding model caching and data residue — does Redwood cache input data or model outputs? for PII we need assurances of non-retention or controlled retention.
[21:52] Priya Menon: good callout — by default we do ephemeral caching for performance (KV cache), but for enterprise customers we can disable caching or apply strict TTLs and ensure PII is not persisted. we'll document cache behavior per model and per deployment mode.

[24:10] Michael Torres: there's a SIG question about incident response and breach notifications — what is your SLA on notifying customers?
[24:20] Jordan Lee: we have an incident response runbook; we notify customers within 72 hours for confirmed data breaches and provide a full post-incident report. for critical incidents we have a faster communication path. we'll attach the IR plan summary.

[26:50] Priya Menon: technical deep-dive offer — if BetaBank wants, we can run a short pen test or provide our third-party pen test report and scope. does BetaBank require proof of pen testing cadence?
[27:05] Michael Torres: yes annual pen tests preferred and details about the scope and remediation timelines are useful.

[29:30] Rajiv Kapoor: legal asks about data residency — if we sign a Dedicated deployment, can all data be guaranteed to never leave our region? Also is there support for on-prem air-gapped?
[29:45] Priya Menon: Dedicated can be pinned to a region, yes, and for on-prem we have an air-gapped packaging option though some operational features like usage analytics require additional integration — we'll highlight constraints in the SIG answers.

[31:20] Anita Desai: about logging integrity — do you provide signed logs or tamper-evident storage?
[31:28] Priya Menon: for Dedicated/private we can recommend using write-once storage or signed logs using customer-managed keys; for hosted we provide append-only storage with immutability flags and exportable checksums. we'll attach the logging integrity whitepaper.

[33:10] Michael Torres: CAIQ specific Q: can you map your controls to the CAIQ control ids? it helps our tooling ingest the responses.
[33:20] Jordan Lee: yes we can provide a CAIQ mapping table and a machine-readable CSV that maps controls to our evidence artifacts. we'll include that in the upload.

[35:45] Priya Menon: one tricky area is backups — encryption of backups and key separation. Redwood encrypts backups with the same AES-256 standard and for BYOK setups the backup encryption keys are managed by the customer's KMS. we'll document how backups are rotated and tested.

[37:30] Anita Desai: do you have any SOC 2 exceptions or scoped exclusions we should be aware of?
[37:36] Jordan Lee: our SOC 2 covers our hosted control plane and the core runtime; any customer-managed private deployments may be out of scope for some controls — we'll flag those as scoped exclusions in the control matrix so BetaBank can assess residual risk.

[39:50] Rajiv Kapoor: on the evidence intake process — what's the recommended way for BetaBank to receive artifacts? secure link, SFTP, or upload to our vendor portal?
[40:00] Jordan Lee: we can provide pre-signed S3 links, or ship a ZIP via an encrypted SFTP to your vendor portal per your preference. we'll align with Rajiv on the delivery method.

[41:30] Michael Torres: can you confirm your change management and patching cadence for infrastructure?
[41:38] Priya Menon: infra patching is CR-driven with monthly security patch windows and emergency patching for critical CVEs. we'll summarize the process and provide a patch history for the past 12 months as evidence.

[44:05] Jordan Lee: ok, quick recap — Action items: Priya will upload SOC 2 redacted and the KMS/HSM integration doc; Jordan will fill the SIG answers and map to CAIQ ids; BetaBank will share the vendor scoring rubric and preferred evidence intake method. schedule follow up tech deep dive for KMS on 2025-03-13. Any final questions?
[44:30] Michael Torres: that's all from our side, thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[44:35] Anita Desai: thanks, we'll review the uploads and get back with any outstanding clarifications.
[44:40] Rajiv Kapoor: thanks, we'll give procurement sign-off once the SOC 2 and the network diagram are received.
[44:48] Jordan Lee: great, we'll send calendar invite for the follow-up and upload the initial evidence within three business days. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

References and shared artifacts noted during call:
- SIG-lite questionnaire (BetaBank version) - will be populated by Jordan and shared via secure folder
- SOC 2 Type II (redacted) - to be attached by Priya
- KMS/HSM integration doc - Priya to upload
- CAIQ/CAIQ mapping CSV - Jordan to attach
- Network architecture / private deployment diagram - Redwood to provide sample, BetaBank to request specifics for their on-prem constraints

Notes on transcription quality: medium; occasional overlap and minor proper-noun mis-hears (e.g., 'K-V case' instead of KV cache) but content preserved.
